result:
**Verdict: PASS** for DG1 round 6 on candidate `sha256:a7b46fbc…210d` (freeze commit `0026a7b`). Both assigned fixes verify, and I raised one new Low finding about stale evidence.

**Candidate check:** HEAD was `f03a9fa`, which is the freeze commit plus metadata-only assignments. The recomputed candidate ID matches. During my run HEAD moved to `1f680fa` when the other reviewers' records were auto-committed. I didn't open those records, and the candidate ID stayed the same.

**What I ran** (in disposable clones under `$TMPDIR`, offline):
- **Build and static checks:** typecheck, build, lint, OpenAPI lint (33 operations), no-CDN, format and contrast all exit 0.
- **Unit tests:** 270/270, including `architecture.test.ts` 77/77.
- **Integration:** run twice on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 database (port 5492). Each run passed 200/200 with all 8 migrations and the getBrandingTokens contract test. Neither database log contains a 57P01, so F-DG1-009 still holds. Audit events cannot be updated, deleted or truncated.
- **End-to-end (port 5493):** 22/22 in English and Arabic, including F-DG1-210 (Lead can edit and archive without a reload). My own earlier F-DG1-210 test also passed in both languages.
- **Acceptance suites:** A12 14/14, A13 5/5, A14 5/5, A18 clean start PASS, A20 token propagation PASS.
- **Validators:** `--register DG1`, `--pipeline`, `--reconcile` and `check-ci-needs` all pass.
- **Requirements:** all 12 are IMPLEMENTED, and every evidence file they cite exists.

**F-DG1-125 → CLOSED_VERIFIED.**
- X6–X8 pass on the candidate. With the pre-fix lint, exactly those three fail, so the new checks do catch the problem.
- A real module file that imports `node:process` makes the module check fail.
- I wrote a 12-case probe of other ways to import the process module (namespace, `require`, dynamic import, re-export and others). All are caught. The global `process.*` forms are still caught, and normal code passes.
- The change only touches the lint and its test. Unit, integration and e2e results are unchanged.

**F-DG1-126 → CLOSED_VERIFIED.**
- The installer suite passes 13 of 14 cases, including AC-10.
- AC-10 fails on the pre-fix installer, so it detects the defect.
- AC-1 (effect) can't run as written here because there is no registry access. I ran an offline version of the same test and it passed.
- AC-10 only checks the root, so I wrote a 5-case probe; all pass:
  - a non-root package does receive its `node_modules`;
  - an excluded package and a publicHoistPattern folder receive nothing;
  - unusual folder names and nested packages work;
  - a package path outside the repo is refused and the install fails safely.

**New finding:**
- **F-DG1-212 (Low, not mandatory, REQ-DLV-042).** The log REQ-DLV-042 cites is the old 13-case run from before the installer fix, and it has no AC-10. D-052 and the fix summary claim "14/14", but no 14-case log is stored anywhere in the repository. This is the same problem as F-DG1-211. The installer itself works; only the evidence is out of date. The fix is to regenerate the log from the current suite somewhere with registry access. I proposed the ID in the QA range; you may renumber it.

**Minor notes, not findings:**
- The X6–X8 test titles say "round-4 lint", but these cases were missed by the round-5 lint.
- If the installer can't parse part of pnpm's output it skips that package instead of failing. A dependency located outside the repo would make every install fail. Neither situation applies to the current repository.

**BLOCKED (not counted as PASS):** both for lack of registry network.
- `pnpm deps:verify`, which wasn't assigned.
- AC-1 (effect) as written; its offline version passed.

Everything is in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG1/round-6/`; open `qa-verifier.md` first. The other records there are `qa-verifier.json`, `qa-verifier.findings.json` and `qa-verifier.verifications.json`. Evidence is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/qa/round-6/`, and my two new probes are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG1/qa/tests/`. The disposable clones have been deleted.
